title: simemu claim liveness breaks across separate ssh invocations (cross-connection, not wrapper churn)
description: Confirmed by fix-simemu 2026-09-07: T-054's ancestor-walk fix (walk past one-shot <shell> -c wrapper processes to the nearest durable ancestor) solves the single-machine wrapper-churn case, but does NOT solve claim liveness across separate ssh studio 'bash -lc ...' invocations from a remote orchestrator machine — each ssh call opens a new connection whose entire remote process tree (sshd handler, bash, simemu) tears down when it returns, so there is no durable remote-side process for PID-based liveness to anchor to no matter how far the ancestor walk goes. Observed directly: simemu claim ios returned expires_at 20min out, but the very next simemu do <session> ... call in a fresh ssh invocation reported session_expired after ~7-13s, every time, across 5+ repro attempts. Two real fixes proposed by fix-simemu: (1) document/support one long-lived ssh session + simemu do <session> renew between long steps as the correct pattern for cross-machine orchestration (works today, no code change) — this is what the T-LU-613 lane used to work around it; (2) if separate ssh 'cmd' invocations should keep working, support SSH ControlMaster/ControlPersist multiplexing so the ancestor-walk lands on the persistent connection process. A simemu do <session> release/simemu release <session> command now exists for explicit cleanup of leaked claims either way.
acceptanceCriteria: Either the multi-ssh-invocation liveness gap is fixed (ControlMaster-aware ancestor walk or equivalent), or it is explicitly documented as unsupported with the long-lived-session + renew pattern as the recommended workaround
A repro test exists: claim via one ssh invocation, do via a second separate ssh invocation, assert the session is NOT reported expired if within its real TTL
